messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: 307800 alerts: cross-region routing anomaly detected. 18% of eu-west2 -> us-east1 requests are being routed to apac regions causing latency spikes and 5xxs. affected cluster: redwood-prod-cc. Auto-escalate to on-call.
jen: seeing the same in dashboards — spike around 12:43 UTC. latency +500ms for a subset of requests. perc 95 -> 1.8s.
mike-sre: paging @nate-oncall. can you take lead? seems like steering policy churn around 12:40.
sara-pd: paging escalation in progress — major incident page sent to on-call. customer impact: partial request failures and timeouts for several EU customers (PLG & some enterprise).
nate-oncall: on it. pulling up recent policy commits, can anyone confirm if there was a promo or operator change rolled at 12:38–12:41?
jen: I saw an internal job push to geo-steer operator at 12:36, flagged for review. commit id: b7c9f2.
jen: copying logs: ```
2026-03-15T12:36:18Z operator:apply commit=b7c9f2 region=eu-west2 policy=latency_favor
2026-03-15T12:38:45Z traffic-shift: new-priority apac over us for fallback
```
mike-sre: that second line looks suspicious — fallback priority got reversed in that commit. probably why eu -> apac now.
alex-sre: can we temporarily pin eu-west2 traffic to eu variants while we roll back? I can push emergency pin if we want.
nate-oncall: yes do that. alex, please apply emergency pin and set TTL low so we can revert quickly. command: ```
redwoodctl steer apply --scope eu-west2 --mode pin --target eu --ttl 30s
```
alex-sre: applying now. will report once done.
incident-bot: action taken by alex-sre: applied steer pin (eu) on redwood-prod-cc. old policy snapshot saved: snap-307800.
alex-sre: pin in place. live metrics show immediate drop in misroutes from 18% -> 1.2%. latency improving.
jen: rolling back operator commit b7c9f2 to previous stable (b6a3d0) to remove the unintended fallback priority change.
mike-sre: agree. if rollback completes, we can remove emergency pin after traffic normalizes. schedule rollback now.
jen: started rollback sequence. command: ```
operatorctl rollback --commit b6a3d0 --target redwood-prod-cc
```
jen: rollback complete. operator config matches pre-release state.
ate-oncall: monitoring... misroutes now ~0.5% and falling. 5xxs track back down to baseline.
customer-success: notified top-5 impacted customers with ETA ~15m for full recovery. linking incident doc in #customer-notify.
mike-sre: to root cause: commit b7c9f2 inadvertently flipped fallback priorities due to a default value change in the policy eval path. looks like a missing test in the operator CI.
jen: filing follow-up: add guarded integration test for fallback-priority invariant, require human review on geo-steer operator changes, and add a preflight check that simulates small-scale rollouts.
alex-sre: will keep the emergency pin for 10 more minutes while we confirm stability, then remove TTL -> normal.
ate-oncall: handing off to alex-sre for next 30m — I'm going offline in 20. brief: rollback done, pin active, metrics stable. please escalate if anything regresses.
alex-sre: ack, taking over. will coordinate with customer-success for final postmortem notes.
mike-sre: postmortem owner assigned: jen. timeline + mitigation steps to be drafted.
jen: quick note for oncall log: severity=SEV2, impact=partial regional misroute causing increased latency and a few 5xxs for EU customers; mitigation=emergency steering pin + operator rollback; RCA=inadvertent fallback priority flip in operator commit.
incident-bot: incident status changed to mitigated by alex-sre. incident channel will remain open for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
customer-success: customers updated: majority back to normal, two customers reported residual cache TTL causing a few more failed requests — advised to flush client caches.
alex-sre: removing emergency pin now (will leave low TTL for 2 more minutes). command: ```
redwoodctl steer remove --scope eu-west2 --mode pin
```
alex-sre: pin removed. metrics remain stable. closing loops.
jen: thanks everyone. follow-up items: add test, CI gating, runbook update for geo-operator rollouts. will schedule postmortem doc and share in #incidents within 24h. :memo:
